/-!
# Erdős Problem 780

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/780](https://www.erdosproblems.com/780)
- [AFL86] Alon, N. and Frankl, P. and Lovász, L., The chromatic number of Kneser hypergraphs. Trans.
  Amer. Math. Soc. (1986), 359-370.
- [Lo78] Lovász, L., Kneser's conjecture, chromatic number, and homotopy. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A
  (1978), 319-324.
-/

namespace Erdos780

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Suppose $n\geq kr+(t-1)(k-1)$ and the edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices
are $t$-coloured. Prove that some colour class must contain $k$ pairwise disjoint edges.

The general case was proved by Alon, Frankl, and Lovász [AFL86].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_780 :
    ∀ k r t n : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → 1 ≤ r → 1 ≤ t →
    k * r + (t - 1) * (k - 1) ≤ n → ∀ c : Finset (Fin n) → Fin t,
      ∃ M ⊆ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).powersetCard r,
        M.card = k ∧ (M : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Pairwise Disjoint ∧
          ∃ b : Fin t, ∀ e ∈ M, c e = b := by
  sorry

end Erdos780

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over colourings of all finite subsets of Fin n, rather than colourings defined only on the r-element edges of the complete hypergraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Membership in univ.powersetCard r is equivalent to having cardinality r. Every total colouring restricts to these edges. Conversely, since 1 ≤ t, every edge-only colouring extends to all finite subsets by assigning colour 0 to non-edges. The matching is required to consist entirely of r-element edges, so the extra colour values cannot affect its cardinality, disjointness, or monochromaticity. A general equivalence between the two formulations was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without using the problem theorem or sorry.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the source's claim. The positive domains, numerical threshold, quantifier scopes, matching cardinality, pairwise disjointness, and common-colour requirement all agree. The research solved tag matches the source. Lean checks confirmed that natural subtraction has the intended meaning under the hypotheses, the hypotheses are satisfiable, and n ≥ r ≥ 1 follows. Independent boundary proofs/tests covered k=1, r=1, and t=1. Exhaustive computation verified all 1,024 two-colourings of the edges of K₅; explicit one-below-threshold colourings correctly fail the matching conclusion. Although the redundant Lovász 1978 reference's full text was inaccessible, its bibliographic details and k=2 attribution were corroborated, and the entire declaration was verified against the exact Erdős source and AFL86. The reviewed file was not modified.
